title: Reconcilement Instruction: Charges a Certificate of Deposit Is Owed for Principal Already Taken Out
content:
A certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line whose ledger shows principal taken out by an early partial withdrawal, with no charge standing against that withdrawal, is owed that charge still, and the charge is booked when the matter is taken up.

## 1. What this governs

What is settled here is the amount of the charge the certificate is owed, the days of interest it stands for, and the ground recorded on it. Nothing is paid out and no other account is touched: the charge lands on the certificate's own ledger, tied to the withdrawal it belongs to, and the principal standing on the certificate falls by it.

## 2. Booking the charge

The action is carried out with the agent-side tool `credit_mischarged_penalty_7001af6d`, which is unlocked and then called by the agent. One call adds a new charge entry to the certificate's ledger, ties it to the withdrawal it belongs to, records the days of interest and the ground on which it is booked, and lowers the principal standing on the certificate by the same amount.

## 3. The values the call takes

| Parameter | What it is |
|---|---|
| `certificate_id` | the reference number of the certificate the charge is booked against, as returned by the certificate lookup for this customer |
| `source_item_id` | the reference number of the single ledger entry this charge belongs to, namely the withdrawal that took the principal out; it is read from the certificate's ledger lookup, which returns each entry's own reference number |
| `entry_amount` | the amount of the charge, in USD to 2 decimal places, always positive, passed as a number already rounded to the cent |
| `entry_days` | the days of interest this charge stands for, written on the entry as a non-negative integer or an empty string, and passed here as a whole integer number of days with no fraction |
| `adjustment_reason` | the ground recorded on the entry |

The value of `adjustment_reason` is one of three. **none** applies where the entry is an ordinary charge raised under the certificate's own terms rather than a correction of the bank's own records. **bank_error** applies where the entry is booked to put right something the bank itself got wrong, including a charge the bank failed to raise at the time. **death_waiver** applies only where estate services have confirmed the owner's death or adjudicated incompetence.

## 4. What comes back

A single confirmation sentence in plain text. It repeats the certificate reference number, the reference number minted for the new charge entry, the reference number of the withdrawal it is tied to, the amount as a USD figure with two decimals, the days of interest as a whole number, and the principal now standing on the certificate as a USD figure with two decimals. Its arrival is what indicates the charge was booked.
